verses.1: And he went there, and then he returns to his homeland. His disciples follow him there.
verses.2: And on the Sabbath day, he began to teach in the synagogue. Many people who heard him were amazed and said, “Where does this wisdom come from? Who gives this person this wisdom? And how are these powers achieved through his hands?”
verses.3: It isn’t this man who is the builder. He is the son of Mary, and also the brother of Jacob, Joseph, Jude, and Simon. And aren’t his sisters also related to us? They were also present among them.
verses.4: And Jesus said to them that a prophet is not worthy of respect unless he lives in his own country, among his own people, and in his own home.
verses.5: And he couldn’t do anything there, unless he treated those few sick people’s wounds.
verses.6: And he was amazed by their incredulity. He also taught the children using circles as a means of teaching.
verses.7: And he invited the twelve. He began to send them out two by two. He gave them the power over the souls of those who were unclean.
verses.8: And he also ordered them not to take anything along on the journey, except for a rod; no bread, no food at all. They were not allowed to bring any copper items with them.
verses.9: But wear sandals, and do not wear two coats at the same time.
verses.10: And he said to them, “When you enter the house, stay there until you leave it.”
verses.11: And if there’s a place where you can’t stand, or if no one listens to you, then move along from there, and put the strap under your feet as a support for them.
verses.12: And when they went out, they called for me to repent.
verses.13: And many demons were driven away from them; they also cured many sick people.
verses.14: And King Herodes heard of his name. It became clear that he was indeed John the Baptist. He said that John the Baptist had risen from the dead, and because of this, the powers within him were active.
verses.15: Others said that it was Elyas. Others said that it was a prophet, like any other prophet.
verses.16: And when Herod heard this, he said, “What have I done to John? He has risen from the dead.”
verses.17: For it was Herodes who sent for John and imprisoned him in prison because Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, had married him.
verses.18: For John said to Herod, “It is not right for you to have a wife from your brother’s family.”
verses.19: But the heroine also wanted to kill him, but she wasn’t able to do so.
verses.20: For Herodes feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man. He also respected him greatly. He listened to many of his teachings with pleasure.
verses.21: And on that happy day, when Herodes prepared a meal for his descendants, for the rulers of his land, for the kings and leaders of Galilee.
verses.22: And when her daughter, Irodias, entered and sang and pleased Heroidus and those who were present with him, the king said to the musician, “Ask me whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
verses.23: And he also promised her that if she asked me to give her half of my kingdom, I would do so.
verses.24: And when she went out, she said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” Her mother replied, “The head of John the Baptist.”
verses.25: And as she entered, she immediately went straight to the king, saying, “I want that the head of John the Baptist be placed on a plate for me.”
verses.26: And because the king became involved in these matters, he did not want to destroy her through those oaths and promises.
verses.27: And immediately after sending out the king’s messenger, he ordered that his head be cut off. Then, after leaving, he executed him in the prison.
verses.28: And he placed his head on the pillow, and handed it to the nurse. The nurse then handed it to his mother.
verses.29: And when the disciples heard this, they came and mourned over him. They also placed him in a tomb.
verses.30: And the apostles gathered around Jesus, and they told him everything they had done and taught.
verses.31: And he said to them, “Go yourselves into the wilderness and rest a little.” For there were many who came and went, and they didn’t have enough food to eat.
verses.32: And they went away on the ship to a desert place of their own.
verses.33: And we saw them coming forward, and many of them were healed. They also came from all the cities, walking along the way, and they gathered around them.
verses.34: And when he came out, he saw a large crowd. He was shocked to see that they were like sheep without a shepherd. So, he began to teach them many things.
verses.35: After many hours had passed, his disciples came to him and said that it was already too late; the place was deserted, and it was already too late.
verses.36: Let them go, so that when they go to the markets and villages, they can decide for themselves what to eat.
verses.37: And the one who answered said to them, “Give us to eat.” They said to him, “Let’s go to the market and buy a hundred dozen vegetables, and then give them to them to eat.”
verses.38: And he said to them, “How many vegetables do you have? Please tell me.” When they heard this, they said, “Five, and two fish.”
verses.39: And he ordered them to bring all of them together in a single assembly, at the grassy field.
verses.40: And they fell very, very far down, by groups of ten and by groups of fifty.
verses.41: And after taking the five fruits and two fish, he looked up to heaven and blessed them. Then he divided the fruits among his disciples, so that they could eat them. He also distributed the two fish to everyone.
verses.42: And they all ate, and they were satisfied.
verses.43: And there were also twelve portions of fish and other seafood.
verses.44: And there were fifty thousand men who ate the vegetables.
verses.45: And immediately, he forced his students to get on the ship and sail towards Bethsaida. He continued to do this until he finally got rid of the crowd there.
verses.46: And after arranging things for them, he went up the mountain to give his instructions.
verses.47: And the ship was located in the middle of the sea; it stood alone on the land.
verses.48: And when they saw that they were being tortured in that torment, for the wind was against them, after four days of imprisonment at night, a storm came towards them as they wandered along the sea. And it seemed that the storm wanted to help them.
verses.49: But those who saw him sailing on the sea thought it was a mirage. They became angry.
verses.50: For we all saw him and were terrified. But he spoke to them immediately, saying, “Do not be afraid. I am here to help you.”
verses.51: And he climbed onto the ship towards them. Then, the wind stopped blowing. They became even more terrified than before.
verses.52: For they did not lie on the bread; rather, their hearts were filled with sorrow.
verses.53: And after crossing over the land, they arrived at Gennareset and went there immediately.
verses.54: And as they got off the ship, they immediately recognized him.
verses.55: They spread throughout the entire region, and they began to move those who were in poor condition to where they were supposed to be.
verses.56: And wherever he went to the markets, cities, or villages during those gatherings, the sick people were seen there. They asked him to touch their clothes with his hand. And those who were touched by his hand were healed.
